name: The prime numbers.
formula: The prime number theorem is the statement that a(n) ~ n * log n as n -> infinity (Hardy and Wright, page 10).
For n >= 2, n*(log n + log log n - 3/2) < a(n); for n >= 20, a(n) < n*(log n + log log n - 1/2). [Rosser and Schoenfeld]
For all n, a(n) > n log n. [Rosser]

name: Fibonacci numbers: F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2) with F(0) = 0 and F(1) = 1.
formula: G.f.: Sum_{n>=0} x^n * Product_{k=1..n} (k + x)/(1 + k*x). - _Paul D. Hanna_, Oct 26 2013

name: a(n) = sigma(n), the sum of the divisors of n. Also called sigma_1(n).
formula: Multiplicative with a(p^e) = (p^(e+1)-1)/(p-1). - _David W. Wilson_, Aug 01 2001
For the following bounds and many others, see Mitrinovic et al. - _N. J. A. Sloane_, Oct 02 2017
If n is composite, a(n) > n + sqrt(n).

name: d(n) (also called tau(n) or sigma_0(n)), the number of divisors of n.
formula: G.f.: Sum_{n >= 1} a(n) x^n = Sum_{k>0} x^k/(1-x^k). This is usually called THE Lambert series (see Knopp, Titchmarsh).

name: Triangular numbers: a(n) = binomial(n+1,2) = n*(n+1)/2 = 0 + 1 + 2 + ... + n.
formula: G.f.: x/(1-x)^3. - _Simon Plouffe_ in his 1992 dissertation

name: Euler totient function phi(n): count numbers <= n and prime to n.
formula: phi(n) = n*Product_{distinct primes p dividing n} (1 - 1/p).
phi(n) = Sum_{d divides n} mu(d)*n/d, i.e., the Moebius transform of the natural numbers; mu() = Moebius function A008683().

name: a(n) is the number of partitions of n (the partition numbers).
formula: G.f.: Product_{k>0} 1/(1-x^k) = Sum_{k>= 0} x^k Product_{i = 1..k} 1/(1-x^i) = 1 + Sum_{k>0} x^(k^2)/(Product_{i = 1..k} (1-x^i))^2.

a(n) - a(n-1) - a(n-2) + a(n-5) + a(n-7) - a(n-12) - a(n-15) + ... = 0, where the sum is over n-k and k is a generalized pentagonal number (A001318) <= n and the sign of the k-th term is (-1)^([(k+1)/2]). See A001318 for a good way to remember this!

name: Number of prime divisors of n counted with multiplicity (also called big omega of n, bigomega(n) or Omega(n)).
formula: Dirichlet g.f.: ppzeta(s)*zeta(s). Here ppzeta(s) = Sum_{p prime} Sum_{k>=1} 1/(p^k)^s. Note that ppzeta(s) = Sum_{p prime} 1/(p^s-1) and ppzeta(s) = Sum_{k>=1} primezeta(k*s). - _Franklin T. Adams-Watters_, Sep 11 2005
